searches.note: Twenty seven searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's; one left unspent. Eleven were restricted to a house's own domain (mastroberardino.com twice, feudi.it twice, montevetrano.it twice, marisacuomo.com twice, villamatilde.it three times) and are read as primary through their summaries; two of the Mastroberardino searches went to the Taurasi rules and one to the archaeological park's tender for the Pompeii vines. No WebFetch was tried. Every record was tested; no fact that rests on no source was kept.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification and its year, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the dates and the rules, then to the sites and the making the author had from the houses' sheets, then to the story beats the author had on one account; a fact the Codex library states stood on the library unless a search contradicted it.

Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a fact the author gave from a house's sheet could not be found again on that house's own domain and a second search did not find it either, it was cut (the Camarato planting year, its harvest time and its years of life).

Sources whose title or address names a living person (a wine wiki under a writer's first name, a photographer's travel site, an interview page under the head of a house) were read in the results but never cited.

tested: Founded 1878: the registration with the Avellino Chamber of Commerce in 1878 by a Cavaliere of the Order of the Crown of Italy (Italia.it, Wein.plus, Wikipedia, which dates him 1850 to 1914 alone), the family's presence in Irpinia from the Bourbon cadastre of the middle of the eighteenth century: confirmed; the man of 1878 stays a forebear, his dates in one source only.
Radici from the 1986 vintage: Wine.com, Palm Bay and Systembolaget give 1986, a merchant's Taurasi Radici 1985 the one exception: confirmed, the author's hedge kept.
The Riserva's site: the highest part of the Montemarano estate at about 550 metres, south east, calcareous clay with stones (the house's 2025 sheet; an older sheet 500 to 650 metres): confirmed.

The making: hand picked in the first ten days of November (the house's 2017 page and 2021 sheet), about thirty months in French barriques and Slavonian casks, then about forty two months in bottle on the newest sheet and forty on the 2021 sheet: confirmed, at least three years kept.
The ageing: sixty years and more on the newest sheet, fifty and more on an older one; no strong vintage named: changed.

The Taurasi rules: DOC by decree of 26 March 1970, DOCG of 11 March 1993, Aglianico at least 85 per cent, the Riserva four years with at least eighteen months in wood counted from 1 December of the harvest year in the text of 2011 (AIS and Regione Campania copies, Quattrocalici): confirmed.

Pompeii: the project begun with the archaeological authorities in 1996, Piedirosso and Sciascinoso, the first wine of the 2001 vintage (Decanter, JancisRobinson.com): confirmed; but the park later chose another group by tender to tend the vines the house had managed (The Buyer, Wine Industry Advisor, Vinetur, The Drinks Business), so the others note was changed.

The division of 1994: one brother kept the name and the Atripalda winery, another the vineyard land and founded Terredora (Uncorked, Wein.plus, Wikipedia); one summary gives 1993 for the division: kept at 1994.
The house rules: nobody living named (the head of the house and the Terredora family stay out); no price or score; no superlative; British spelling; no dash.

changed.now: the house's newest sheet speaks of sixty years and more.
changed.why: The 2025 sheet gives sixty years and more and an older sheet fifty and more; neither ties the figure to a strong vintage.

tested: Founded 1986 by two families of the province at Sorbo Serpico (Escapement Magazine, Decanter, the library): confirmed.

The winery of 2004 by a Japanese architect, with interiors by a designer couple (the house's Discover our winery page and its shop's tour pages): confirmed; the architect and her partner are living and stay unnamed.

Pietracalda: Sorbo Serpico, 400 to 600 metres, clay and limestone, stainless steel at 16 to 18 degrees Celsius, about five months on the lees with repeated stirring (the English sheet; four to five on the Japanese page), twelve months on the lees and three in bottle for the Riserva of 2022 (its Italian sheet): confirmed; the vineyard's size and the vines' age stay out as volatile.
Fiano di Avellino: DOC by decree of 27 April 1978, DOCG of 18 July 2003, the Riserva twelve months counted from 1 November (the AIS copy of the rules, Federvini, Italian Wine Central): confirmed.
The story's later vintages labelled Riserva rested on one sheet for one vintage: changed.
The house rules: no family member named, no living architect named, no price, no score, no superlative, British spelling, no dash.

changed.was: Later vintages of Pietracalda were labelled Riserva and kept a full year on their lees, by the house's own sheet for the 2022.
changed.now: The house's sheet for the 2022 vintage labels Pietracalda a Riserva, kept a full year on its lees.
changed.why: Only the sheet for the 2022 vintage gives the Riserva; the English sheet and the Japanese page give the plain wine about five months on its lees, so the record no longer says every later vintage is a Riserva.

tested: The first vintages: the 1991 bottled only for friends, the 1992 and 1993 after it, 1993 the first commercial vintage and released in 1995 by one account (Superiore.de, Best of Wines, the estate's home page and vintage pages): confirmed; the table line's sold from 1993 changed.

The friends of the middle of the 1980s: the estate's home page gives a group of wine lovers, with the future consultant oenologist among them, and its people page calls him an old friend who later became a known oenologist; one account has him hired only for the 1992 vintage: the story's consultant who advised the planting changed.
The blend: about six parts Cabernet Sauvignon, three of Merlot and one of Aglianico, varying by vintage (the estate's sheets, Best of Wines): confirmed.

The making: steel after drawing off about fifteen per cent of the must, about twenty days of fermentation and maceration, 225 litre barriques of Nevers, Allier and Tronçais oak for eight to fourteen months by vintage, new in the earlier vintages, and at least six months in bottle (the 2017 and 2018 sheets and the vintage pages from 1996 to 2012): confirmed; south west aspect on the 2017 sheet: confirmed.

The house rules: the founder and the consultant are living and stay unnamed (the founder is in people.json; the consultant is not); the critic's nickname for the wine is not used; no price or score; no superlative; British spelling; no dash.

Costa d'Amalfi DOC of 1995 (the house's Azienda page with the author's AIS copy), subzones Furore, Ravello and Tramonti (the library): confirmed; the house makes Ravello and plain Costa d'Amalfi wines as well (its wine pages), so the story's the house's wines carry the Furore name changed.

tested: The revival: the 1960s, a lawyer with a passion for old wines and the Latin authors, collaborators who included professors of the Faculty of Agriculture of the University of Naples, stock that had survived phylloxera at the end of the nineteenth century replanted on the Massico (the house's history page; Winedering and FIRSTonline for the lawyer and the 1960s): confirmed.
The name: the house's history page names the estate for the founder's wife: added, the author had it on one account.
The wine's eclipse: the house says the wine had dropped out of production by the early twentieth century; the record's vanished for centuries changed.
The second generation in 1985 (the house's history page): confirmed.

The first vintages: the Falerno del Massico Rosso of 1975, partly in new Allier barriques and partly in Slavonian casks of 10 to 35 hectolitres for ten to twelve months (the house's Rosso sheet); Vigna Camarato of 1981, Aglianico 80 per cent with Piedirosso, twelve to eighteen months in Allier barriques by thirds new, second and third use, then twelve to eighteen months in bottle, only in the best years, at San Castrese in Sessa Aurunca (the house's Vigna Camarato sheet, Bottle of Italy): confirmed.

The Camarato planting of 1965, the harvest in the last ten days of October and fifteen to twenty years of life: not found in two searches, one restricted to the house's domain; the Rosso sheet gives vineyards of various years from 1963 to 2000 and a listing gives 1965 as the company's founding: cut.

Falernian: the Ager Falernus, the plain below the Massicus, the Opimian vintage of 121 BC served at a banquet of 60 BC by Pliny's account, Horace's Odes and Martial's epigrams (Wikipedia, the Wein.plus glossary); only Wikipedia names a Mount Falernus: the Mons Falernus of old changed.
The DOC of 1989 for Sessa Aurunca, Cellole, Mondragone, Falciano del Massico and Carinola in Caserta province, with a white, a red and a Primitivo (the AIS copy of the rules, Wein.plus): confirmed.

The house rules: the founder is described for want of two sources for his dates; his children, grandson and the family are living and stay unnamed; no price, score or superlative; British spelling; no dash.

changed.why: The accounts read put Falernian in the Ager Falernus, the plain below the Massicus; only one names a Mount Falernus, so the Latin name is not given.
